chapter_title: The Chapter of the Man who asks: Why [am] I someti

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
There are states in which the will rests in quiet delight because the understanding is turned to what builds, and all the truths that have been learned stand in right order. Then the life of use proceeds evenly, and instruction goes out to others in a gentle form; the inner life is glad in enlightened intelligence, and even the outer life feels unburdened because the interior is in wisdom and genuine knowing.

Yet there are states in which unrest seizes a person. Truths lose their arrangement, and obscurity thickens together with a crowd of contrary affections—grief, anger, envy, and craving. Then a person strains to bring them into obedience, but in that moment no power of understanding is found to subject them, because they surge up with force. Perverse persuasions and evil intentions then come into action and torment the mind, so that nothing in them is coherent or distinctly formed. It becomes uncertain whether such disorder is being uncovered so it may be seen, or whether it has been admitted from without and driven inward; it is also uncertain whether it has awakened from one’s own selfhood and risen in rebellion against what is better. Only this is clearly perceived: the whole doctrine of life is thrown into confusion. Then uses are performed without right aim, teaching loses weight and truth in expression, and a person becomes an occasion of trouble and obscurity to those conjoined in charity. Even the outer life reacts against the inner disorder and falls into infirmity for that period.

This can be made plain. When the inner life is joined to the outer and an enlightened understanding comes, then by the power of wisdom in obedience the mind is purified and the life is cleansed and made new in form. In that renewal there is no unrest, no confusion, and no disturbance.

But when disturbance arises, unrest enters first through fixed tendencies and compulsions in the natural level—hereditary and acquired patterns that press and agitate the person into craving, anger, heaviness, and grief, according to the inclination then chosen. Moreover, insofar as that inclination invites it, influences from the spiritual environment trouble the person through the points of attachment by which the mind is conjoined to such influx.

There are also times when those higher influences are quiet and do not press, yet disorder still comes in through what is appropriated into the natural life and made one with it. Then irritation and confusion increase again, and anger and craving multiply with heaviness and grief, because what is admitted carries contentious and impure qualities. These are received into the outer life along with what is appropriated, and they join themselves to the evils and falsities already there; thus they transmit into the mind anger and craving, heaviness and grief, as impulses arising from the outer level.

But there are also times when what is appropriated is clean and rightly ordered, with more of what is living and enlightened in it and less of what is dead and harmful, and then evil influence is diminished. In such a state even the surrounding natural condition becomes still as the outer level is clarified, and the inner form is quieted from disturbance. Peace increases through the good that is made one with the person, and one is found at ease because the inner dwellings are better governed by the living element that then predominates through the illumination of those who are in a completed state of use and purification. In them the demand of guilt is ended, and the inner life is unburdened because it is conjoined with living goods and truths present with the person. Therefore these calm states are found within, and they pass through into act without causing trouble; the outer life flourishes, uses become determinate and well constructed in that same order, truths are restored to their places, teaching proceeds rightly, and the inner life is free, rising into higher thought.

This is the settling of the matter: whence come the bitter intentions and disorderly reasonings that trouble, and whence come good intentions and gentle ordered truths when the understanding is quiet. When the outer level is agitated, trouble is induced through lower avenues by impure elements that are admitted and appropriated; but when the higher avenues are quiet, what is appropriated is also clear and pure, and then the will is found set in right order and the counsels of the mind rest in peace without disturbance.

paragraph_translations.translation: There are states in which the will is peaceful and inwardly glad because the understanding is turned to what builds, and all the truths that have been learned stand arranged in right order. Then the life of use proceeds straightforwardly, and instruction goes out to others in a gentle form. The inner person rests in delight within enlightened intelligence, and even the outer life feels unburdened because the interior is in wisdom and genuine knowing.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: Establishes the ordered, peaceful state of the regenerated mind in action and speech.

Then the person struggles with all strength to subject these things, yet in that hour no power of understanding is found that can bring them into obedience, because they surge up with force. Perverse persuasions and evil intentions then come into action and torment the mind, so that nothing is coherent or distinctly formed within the counsel. It becomes uncertain whether this disorder is being uncovered so it may be seen, or whether it has been admitted from without and driven inward, or whether it has awakened from one’s own selfhood and risen in rebellion against what is better. Only this is perceived clearly: the whole doctrine of life is badly confused. Then uses are performed in error and disturbance, teaching becomes worthless in expression, and the will finds no rest; one becomes a source of trouble and obscurity to those conjoined in charity. Even the outer life reacts against the inner disorder and falls into infirmity for that period.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: Introduces the contrasting state of temptation-like confusion and its effects on use and community.

paragraph_translations.translation: The question is rightly put, and the matter can be opened. When the inner life is joined to the outer and an enlightened understanding comes to it, then by the power of wisdom in obedience the mind is purified and the life is cleansed and made new in form. In that renewal there is no unrest, no confusion, and no disturbance.
paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS: Moves from description of states to a doctrinal explanation of purification and renewal.

paragraph_translations.translation: But when disturbance arises and a person is troubled, the unrest enters in many ways. First it comes through fixed tendencies and compulsions in the natural level—hereditary and acquired patterns that press and agitate the person into craving, anger, heaviness, and grief, according to the inclination then chosen. Also, insofar as that inclination invites it, influences from the spiritual environment trouble the person through the points of attachment by which the mind is conjoined to them.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: Specifies primary sources of disturbance as innate/formed dispositions and invited spiritual influx.
paragraph_translations.notes: The astrological framing resists direct spiritual rendering; it has been taken as compulsive natural tendencies and patterned pressures acting through attachment points.

paragraph_translations.translation: Again, there are times when higher influences are quiet and do not press, yet disorder still enters by what is appropriated into the natural life and made one with it. paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: Adds a second avenue of disturbance—appropriation that mingles with existing evils in the outer life.
paragraph_translations.notes: The talk of mixtures and ingestion has been translated as appropriation of qualities into the natural degree; some specificity is inevitably generalized.

paragraph_translations.notes: The segment about ‘justified souls’ and ‘dues’ is slightly opaque; rendered as completed purification and ended guilt-demand, but the exact doctrinal nuance may vary.

paragraph_translations.translation: Thus the matter is determined: whence come the bitter intentions and disorderly reasonings that trouble, and whence come good intentions and gentle ordered truths when the understanding is quiet. When the outer level is agitated, trouble is induced through lower avenues by impure elements that are admitted and appropriated; but when the higher avenues are quiet, what is appropriated is also clear and pure. Then the will is found set in right order, and the counsels of the mind rest in peace without disturbance.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: Concludes by summarizing the sources of disorder and peace as lower versus higher avenues of influence and appropriation.
paragraph_translations.notes: The language of ‘conduits above/below’ has been translated as higher and lower avenues of influx between inner and outer levels.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Strong coherence as a single teaching on alternating states of spiritual order and disorder: peace from rightly ordered truths and obedient wisdom; disturbance from compulsive natural tendencies, invited environmental influx, and impure appropriation that joins existing evils. The main stumble is the astrological/physiological idiom, which requires generalizing into patterns of natural compulsion and appropriated qualities, but the progression remains consistent from experience → cause → resolution.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential substrate: the chapter opens with an experiential alternation (peace vs turmoil) explained in terms of inner order/disorder and their functional effects on speech, works, community, and bodily condition. No intrusive jurisdictional catalogues or rank-lists appear.
findings.evidence: Text teaches by states and effects: “my doctrines are ordered and in place… I utter my words… with sweetness… Even my body is carefree” (¶2) versus “My doctrines are confused… grief and anger and envy and lust… my word is worthless… I become a source of trouble… Even my body rises up against me” (¶3). The spiritual reading reports “Strong coherence as a single teaching on alternating states,” and it does not stumble here; the spiritual sense arises directly from function (order → right speech/use; disorder → incoherence and bodily reaction).

findings.diagnosis: Mostly correspondential, with a mild institutional phrasing that can sound like a later Mani-layer formula (“wisdom and obedience”) but it is integrated into the functional explanation (purification → new man → no disturbance). Not an insertion that breaks narrative flow.
findings.evidence: The paragraph answers the lived problem by a functional process: “when the Light Mind will come to it, shall be purified… and… made a new man. There is no trouble…” (¶6). The spiritual reading marks this as a doctrinal explanation that still fits: “Moves from description of states to a doctrinal explanation of purification and renewal.” The phrase “power of wisdom and obedience” is slightly slogan-like, but it does not introduce named authorities, territorial ranks, or a detached inventory; removing it would not improve narrative coherence.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty: an astrological causal scheme (“birth-signs… difficult stars… powers of heaven… roots”) sits in the middle of an otherwise psychological/ethical correspondential teaching. The spiritual reading explicitly stumbles and has to generalize the idiom into “compulsive natural tendencies” and “spiritual environment.” This is not administrative (no jurisdictions, stations, ranks), but it is a foreign explanatory register that stresses the correspondential reading.
findings.evidence: Astrological mechanism: “first through his birth-signs and his difficult stars… Also… the powers of heaven… through their roots, to which he is attached” (¶7). The reading admits resistance: “The astrological framing resists direct spiritual rendering; it has been taken as compulsive natural tendencies…” That is exactly the stumble: the text explains disturbance by stellar determinants rather than by functional inner movements alone. However, narratively it still advances the chapter’s question “whence come” disturbance, so excising is not justified on coherence grounds.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential development using physiological ingestion as functional causality (what enters/joins the body produces thoughts/affections). The reader’s note that it must be ‘generalized’ is a hermeneutic accommodation, not evidence of a textual insertion.
findings.evidence: The teaching proceeds by function: “a difficult part comes into him by the nourishment… mixed… joined in with the wicked parts of the body… transferring the anger… lust… depression… grief” (¶8). The spiritual reading: “talk of mixtures and ingestion has been translated as appropriation… some specificity is inevitably generalized,” but it does not claim a narrative break; the causal chain remains coherent (intake → mixture → joining → mental effects). No administrative markers appear.

findings.diagnosis: Possible seam-expansion within an otherwise coherent correspondential paragraph: the clause about “justified souls,” “dues,” and allied “living souls” introduces a mini-doctrinal aside that shifts from functional physiology/atmosphere imagery to a quasi-legal/accounting register (“dues”) and collective-personal entities (“justified souls… allied”). The spiritual reading stumbles here as ‘opaque.’ This looks like a secondary clarification/gloss embedded in a functional description, but it is not clearly detachable without risking loss of meaning.
findings.evidence: Voice shift inside ¶10: after functional statements (“nourishment… pure… greater in light and life… atmosphere… purified… peace increases”), the text pivots: “because of the living part… on account of the light of these justified souls… The ones that have perfected their deeds. Their dues have ceased… allied with these living souls” (¶10). The spiritual reading flags it: “segment about ‘justified souls’ and ‘dues’ is slightly opaque; rendered as… ended guilt-demand.” That opacity corresponds to a register change (legal/communal justification language) that is not motivated by the food/air mechanism. Still, the paragraph remains thematically tied (why peace increases) and removing it does not obviously make the argument smoother, because the text uses it to explain *why* the “living part” predominates.
findings.scope: Annotate within ¶10 the aside beginning with “because of the living part, which is greater on account of the light of these justified souls…” through “…they have been allied with these living souls that [are p]resent in you.” as a likely doctrinal gloss/overlay in a different register inside a correspondential description.

findings.diagnosis: Clean summary/conclusion that re-stitches the chapter’s causal explanation into a two-way schema (“conduits below” vs “conduits above”). The imagery is consistent with correspondential teaching (pathways/avenues of influx and appropriation), and the spiritual reading does not report a narrative stumble here.
findings.evidence: The conclusion explicitly answers the opening question: “Whence come these bad counsels… and… these good counsels… I have told you…” (¶11). It summarizes by functional channels: “troubled by the conduits… below… by food… Again, when the conduits above are calmed… food… clear and pure” (¶11). The reader’s note frames this cleanly as “higher and lower avenues of influx,” indicating coherence rather than intrusion.

textual_criticism.summary: Findings: 6. Clear correspondential substrate dominates (¶2–3, ¶8, ¶11). One genuine difficulty (¶7) where an astrological causal idiom forces the spiritual reading to generalize but does not break narrative coherence; no excision recommended. One likely embedded gloss/overlay in ¶10 (“justified souls… dues… allied”) where register shifts and the reading reports opacity; recommended action is annotate (not excise) because it is intertwined with the paragraph’s explanation and is not a detachable administrative block.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: Sometimes [I] am peaceful in my heart, as my consideration [is constructive], and all my doctrines are ordered and in place. I conduct [straightway in] my works, as I utter my words to all people with sweetness. I am peaceful of heart in the gladness of the Mind. ⟨p.214⟩ Even my body is carefree, and my soul [rejo]ices in wisdom and true knowledge.

There are also times when I shall be troubled. My doctrines are confused. Gloom increases with them, and grief and anger and envy and lust. I am troubled, struggling with all my might that I would subdue them; not finding the strength of mind to subdue them at that hour nor day when they surged up in me. And all these evil teachings and wicked considerations come forth. They have tormented me. I do not comprehend, because there is no single shape in all these counsels that have entered me. Are they revealed to me, or indeed did they enter me from outside and have been shaken into me? I do not know if they have wakened within me alone, have rebelled inside me and set themselves up against me. I do not know about that. However, this only I understand: that I shall be very badly confused in all my doctrines. I shall do [error and disturbance] in my works, and you find my word is worthless in my mouth. I shall not find how [to be at peace in my heart], and I become a source of trouble and confusion for my brothers. Even my body rises up against me, and sickens for that entire day.

Well do you ask about this lesson. Behold, I will explain it to you! ⟨p.215⟩ Understand this: The soul that assumes the body, when the Light Mind will come to it, shall be purified by the power of wisdom and obedience, and it is cleansed and made a new man. There is no trouble in (the soul), nor confusion nor disturbance.

However, when a disturbance will arise for him and he will be troubled, this disturbance shall go into him in [many ways], first through his birth-signs and his difficult stars that [press upon him;] they turn over him and stir him and trouble him with lust and anger and depression and grief, as he wills. Also, as he wills, the powers of heaven shall trouble him through their roots, to which he is attached.

Again, there are times you shall find the powers of heaven are peaceful and tranquil for him, and it comes to [another way; though] a difficult part comes into him by the nourishment that he has eaten, or else indeed in some [mixture of herbs] or in the water that they have drunk. Again, trouble and confusion and anger will increase in him, and lust multiplies upon him together with depression and grief; because of the nourishment of the bread he has eaten and the water he has drunk, which are full of bothersome parts, a vengeful counsel. They shall enter his body, [mixed in] with these foods, and they even become joined in with the wicked parts of the body and the sin that is in him; transferring the anger and the lust and the depression and the grief, these wicked thoughts of the body.

There are times, however, if you shall find that the nourishment that comes into you is pure [and well blended], so it is greater in light and life while the waste is less in it, and the evil-doing is diminished from it. Even the atmosphere above is still, being purified through the [pure air and clear wind;] also the image is calmed from [every disturbance; and peace] increases in you through ⟨p.216⟩ those good parts of the food that come into you. And they find you at ease and tranquil, as you are well governed in your abodes because of the living part, which is greater on account of the light of these justified souls that are in it. The ones that have perfected their deeds. Their dues have ceased, while their soul is carefree [are sweet in your mouth;] they have been allied with these living souls that [are p]resent in you. Due to this you shall find them in you, calm in tranquillity, and they come from you without trouble; and you are found flourishing of body. Even your deeds are determined, being well constructed after their manner, and your doctrines are in order, as your words [because] your soul is carefree within you, ascending like a bird.

Behold, I have explained to you the determination of this lesson for which you asked: Whence come these bad counsels and considerations into you, these vengeful thoughts that trouble; and also whence come into you these good counsels and sweet doctrines, when your Mind is calmed for you. I have told you that when [your bo]dy is troubled, you shall be troubled by the conduits of they below, the difficult parts that come into you by food and the act of eating. Again, when the conduits above are calmed from you, even your food that has come into you is clear and pure. Your heart shall be found ordered in its place, your counsels at peace from disturbance.

changes_summary: No changes made. The only critic action was an annotate recommendation within ¶10 (Finding 5), which per rules does not modify the chapter text. All other findings recommended none.
